items.title: Jackie Williams interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: I was introduced to the teacher. His names was Mr. Brooks... he taught the rudiments of music, you know, not only the drums he taught theory and all the scales and everything

ctx.x: I’ve been wondering about that. Well I guess I was always destined to be one I guess, although I like music, I was just infatuated with music for as long as I could remember from a kid. I was always, you know kids roll up paper and blow in it imitating a horn or they’d be beating on something. So I was always fascinated with music. I could remember — I liked almost every instrument I heard. And I could remember listening, staying up nights, you know, listening, with my ear glued to the radio listening to music.…

never forget him, Aubrey Brooks. And he gave all the kids a wonderful little like screening, you know, to see what talent they had. So I told him I would like to study some drums, you know. So he was showing me a few things. This is the pad, he started out with the pad and as time went on, we had the classes there, he taught the rudiments of music, you know, not only the drums he taught theory and all the scales and everything, which was so wonderful.
